title: feat: attach model health to /v1/models and /models by default
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary
- Reintroduces the `health` field removed by #15052, but by default on every entry (no `?status=` opt-in)
- Reuses the same cached Tinybird fetch as `GET /models/status` (`cf.cacheTtl`), so no extra Tinybird load
- A missing/failing feed degrades every model to `health.status: "unknown"` instead of 502ing discovery

## Shape
```json
"health": { "status": "healthy", "success_rate": 99.4, "requests": 48213 }
```
Flat, closer to OpenRouter's per-endpoint uptime fields than the old nested `window_minutes`/`checked_at`/`stale` object. The window (24h) is documented once on the route instead of repeated per entry. `requests` doubles as a rough popularity signal.

## Test plan
- [x] `biome check` clean on all touched files
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` shows zero errors on touched files
- [ ] Vitest suite couldn't run in this checkout (pre-existing stale `node_modules`/miniflare compat-flag failure, reproduces on unrelated test files too — unrelated to this diff)
- [ ] Manual `curl /v1/models` after staging deploy

gist.headline: The model shelf has vitals
gist.blurb: Model discovery now comes with a tiny health check attached. The hive can see which models are humming along, plus their 24-hour success rate and request count.
gist.summary: The /v1/models and /models discovery endpoints now include a cached per-model health object by default, with 24-hour status, success_rate, and requests fields sourced from the same Tinybird cache used by /models/status.
gist.impact: Developers can choose models with immediate visibility into health and rough popularity, while a missing health feed safely returns health.status as "unknown" instead of interrupting model discovery.
